title: Design Background Job Processing in ASP.NET Core
description: Offload long-running work from HTTP requests using hosted services, queues, and external job processors.

data.text: Users upload large CSV files for processing. Parsing takes 30+ seconds. Design a system that does not block the web request and survives app restarts.
Use BackgroundService for lightweight, in-process background work. Simple but loses jobs on restart and does not scale across instances.

data.title: BackgroundService with Channel

data.text: Hangfire or a message broker like RabbitMQ/Kafka survives restarts, supports retries, and provides a dashboard for monitoring.

data.title: Hangfire Integration

data.text: Separate the web API from the worker. The API publishes messages to RabbitMQ or Kafka. A standalone worker service consumes them.

data.title: RabbitMQ Producer and Consumer
When to Use What
data.text: Use BackgroundService for simple fire-and-forget within the same app. Use Hangfire when you need retries, persistence, and monitoring. Use a message broker for large-scale, multi-service decoupled systems.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: BackgroundService is simplest but not durable across restarts
Hangfire adds persistence, retries, and a dashboard with minimal code
Message brokers decouple producers from consumers completely
Always separate concerns: web API should not do heavy processing inline
Use Channels for in-process producer-consumer patterns
data.takeaway: Offloading work from HTTP requests keeps your API responsive and scalable. Choose the simplest tool that meets your durability and observability needs.
